builder_attribution: Gene Andre / Andre Audio-Tronics relationship remains temporally unresolved
key_finding: Tone Machines documents Gene Andre working at Ampeg from 1964 and opening Andre Audio-Tronics in 1969, while the later ANDRE trademark record lists first use in commerce as 1973. Therefore the 1960s East Coast Fuzz 'Andre' identity should not automatically be labeled as a 1969-corporate Andre Audio-Tronics product without direct specimen or advertisement evidence.

USPTO-derived trademark record for ANDRE, filed September 22 1975, identifies Andre Audio-Tronics, Inc. at 350 W. 49th St., New York and covers amplifiers, PA systems, and electronic sound effects including reverb, fuzz tone, tremolo, phase shifter, vibrator, and mixers; first use in commerce is listed as August 1 1973.

Fuzzboxes identifies E.U. Wurlitzer / Tim's Own as a Boston marketed identity in the East Coast family. A surviving example has a 20th-week-1967 pot code, establishing period existence but not factory attribution.

A surviving 1968 Tim's Own Fuzzer Buzzer is documented with 1968 pot dates. Fuzzboxes treats E.U. Wurlitzer [Tim's own] as one identity, so the archive should avoid counting Tim's Own and E.U. Wurlitzer as automatically independent factories or even necessarily independent marketed labels.

Effects Database groups an East Coast Mica-Tone Fuzz with Manny's and related two/three-knob East Coast forms, while independent Japanese Super-Fuzz references document Mica Tone as a Shin-Ei-related marketed identity. These must remain separate records unless a specific specimen proves otherwise.

builder_attribution: Schaller or Hofner-related production remains unresolved
key_finding: A specialist fuzz timeline identifies a German-built Hofner Buzz Tone and states the same pedal was marketed as Halifax Buzz Tone. This conflicts with the East Coast family databases that list a separate Halifax Fuzz related to Clark/MGI. The archive should not merge the German Halifax Buzz Tone and East Coast Halifax Fuzz without specimen-level reconciliation.
